module: FA COPD and Asthma Parts III-V

questions.question: A 63-year-old patient with 40 prior pack-years of smoking presents with exertional dyspnea. She had three prior hospitalizations in the last year for COPD exacerbations, and she is managed with a combined albuterol and ipratropium inhaler. On exam, oxygen saturation is 91% on room air and lungs are clear to auscultation. Office spirometry demonstrates an FEV1 = 1.20 L (30% predicted) with FEV1/FVC ratio = 0.50 and 13% improvement in FEV1 after bronchodilator administration. The chest roentgenogram shows apical bullous changes and hyperinflation without parenchymal disease. Which one of the following options in therapy is best suited for this patient?
options: Add a low dose of oral corticosteroids daily
Add salmeterol-fluticasone and tiotropium and change combination albuterol and ipratropium to albuterol rescue inhaler
Continue current albuterol-ipratropium therapy, using nebulizer as administration route
questions.explanation: This patient has severe COPD with exacerbations creating a need for one or more long-acting bronchodilators and inhaled corticosteroids to prevent repeat hospitalization. Supplemental oxygen would not be indicated with oxygen saturation above 88%, and oral corticosteroid therapy is to be avoided if inhaled therapies adequately control the patient. Nebulizer is not superior to MDI with a spacer.

questions.question: Heliox has been used as a treatment in severe asthma exacerbation. Which of the following statements is/are true?

statements.label: A
statements.text: Heliox is a bronchodilator

statements.label: B
statements.text: Heliox reduces the resistance load and thus reduces the work of breathing

statements.label: C
statements.text: Heliox should be used in patients requiring FiO2 > 50%

statements.label: D
statements.text: The beneficial effect of Heliox is due to its low density

questions.explanation: Heliox is a low-density gas mixture of 60-80% helium and 20-40% oxygen, that has been proposed as a potential therapy in patients with acute exacerbation of COPD and asthma. Several studies have shown that Heliox breathing reduces air flow resistance in patients with obstructive lung disease, enhances the bronchodilation effect of salbutamol and has beneficial effects in severe asthma attacks. Heliox may also reduce the work of breathing and improve pulmonary gas exchange efficiency. Heliox is not indicated in patients requiring high FiO2, as the benefit of low density is lost at a FiO2 level above 0.4.

questions.question: The mechanisms of worsening of preexisting hypercapnia by excessive oxygen administration in COPD patients are:

statements.label: A
statements.text: Increase in physiologic dead space

statements.label: B
statements.text: Attenuation of hypoxic ventilatory drive

statements.label: C
statements.text: Haldane effect

statements.label: D
statements.text: Ventilation-perfusion inequality

questions.explanation: The mechanism of oxygen-induced hypercapnia was formerly thought to be oxygen-induced inhibition of ventilatory drive in patients considered to be critically dependent on the hypoxic ventilatory drive, as are patients with severe COPD. However, physiological studies have shown that during acute exacerbation of severe COPD, the respiratory drive remains markedly increased even after oxygen administration and despite an increase in PaCO2. The mechanism of oxygen-induced hypercapnia is now better understood as having two key components: the Haldane effect, and impaired hypoxic pulmonary vasoconstriction. In patients with severe COPD, a decrease in alveolar oxygen tension normally results in hypoxic pulmonary vasoconstriction via local mediators. A high FiO2 increases alveolar oxygen tension and inhibits this vasoconstriction, leading to increased ventilation-perfusion mismatch and increased physiologic dead space. The Haldane effect refers to the phenomenon whereby increasing arterial PO2 reduces the blood's capacity to carry CO2 (as Hb-bound carbamino compounds or as bicarbonate), thereby increasing the partial pressure of dissolved CO2.

questions.question: Systemic corticosteroids (SC) are considered as standard therapy in acute exacerbation of COPD. Which of the following statements is correct:
options: Intravenous is the preferred route of administration.
50 mg of prednisolone as a single morning dose, or 200 mg of hydrocortisone in divided doses, are adequate for most patients
50 mg of prednisolone as single morning dose, or 100 mg of methylprednisolone in divided doses, are adequate for most patients
Long course therapy with SC (>7 days) is more efficient than short course as has been associated with a decreased rate of hospitalization for acute exacerbation
In patients with acute exacerbation of COPD admitted in ICU, the recommended doses of SC are lower than that for patients treated as outpatients or in the ward
questions.explanation: [UNCONFIRMED] The source screenshot marked a different option as the selected (incorrect) answer and did not visibly highlight which option was correct; no option's wording matched the feedback text verbatim. The feedback states: daily doses of corticosteroids equivalent to 50 mg prednisolone as a single morning dose, or 200 mg hydrocortisone in divided doses, are adequate for most patients. The dosing-schedule wording of this option has been corrected from the source's 'twice a day' to 'as a single morning dose' to match the feedback text exactly (source text internally contradicted itself). Lower-dose strategies are also suggested for patients admitted to the ICU, as they have been associated with reduced hospital and ICU length of stay, reduced hospital cost, reduced duration of invasive ventilation, and reduced need for insulin therapy and fewer fungal infections. Oral rather than intravenous corticosteroids is the preferred route of administration, even for patients hospitalised due to a COPD exacerbation. Randomised data support a short-course (5-7 day) strategy for systemic corticosteroid administration. Verify against the original ESICM material if possible.

questions.question: Which of the following treatments for exacerbation of asthma is NOT a standard therapy?
questions.explanation: Inhaled short-acting beta-agonists, systemic corticosteroids, supplemental oxygen and inhaled anticholinergics are all standard components of asthma exacerbation management. Antibiotics are not routinely indicated, since most asthma exacerbations are triggered by viral infection or allergen exposure rather than bacterial infection, and should be reserved for patients with clear evidence of bacterial infection.

questions.question: Methylxanthines have been proposed as therapy in patients with acute exacerbation of COPD and asthma. Which of the following statements is/are true?

statements.label: A
statements.text: Methylxanthines are potent phosphodiesterase inhibitors and adenosine receptor agonists.

statements.label: B
statements.text: Aminophylline is strongly recommended as a standard therapy in all patients with exacerbation of COPD and asthma

statements.label: C
statements.text: Combination of SABA and aminophylline do not improve patient's outcome compared to SABA alone

statements.label: D
statements.text: In patients with near-fatal asthma or life-threatening asthma and an inadequate response to initial therapy, intravenous aminophylline should be considered as a potential therapy

questions.explanation: Methylxanthines are potent phosphodiesterase inhibitors and adenosine receptor antagonists (not agonists) that have a direct bronchodilatory effect, mainly at doses achieving relatively high serum levels. Currently, methylxanthines are not included as part of standard therapy in patients with acute asthma, due to both low efficacy and a high rate of severe side-effects. Add-on treatment with aminophylline does not improve outcome compared to SABA alone. However, in some patients with near-fatal or life-threatening asthma and an inadequate response to initial therapy, intravenous aminophylline should be considered as a potential therapy. The suggested dose is a loading dose of 5 mg/kg over 20 minutes (if the patient is not on oral maintenance therapy) followed by a continuous infusion of 0.5-0.7 mg/kg/hr.

questions.question: In acute exacerbation of COPD (AECOPD) initial management includes:

statements.label: A
statements.text: Supplemental oxygen to achieve SaO2 88-92%, and bronchodilators administered with nebulizer driven by oxygen (FiO2 1.0)

statements.label: B
statements.text: Supplemental oxygen to achieve SaO2 88-92% at required flow and nebulized bronchodilators with nebulizer driven by room air.

statements.label: C
statements.text: Supplemental oxygen (FiO2 1.0) initially administered at 8 to 10 L/min and bronchodilators administered with nebulizer driven by oxygen (FiO2 1.0)

statements.label: D
statements.text: Supplemental oxygen (FiO2 1.0) initially administered at 8 to 10 L/min and bronchodilators administered with nebulizer driven by room air.

questions.explanation: Patients with AECOPD often present at the ED with hypoxaemia and/or hypercapnia. Administration of a high concentration of oxygen is associated with a potential risk of PaCO2 elevation. In patients with AECOPD, targeted oxygen therapy to achieve SaO2 88-92%, with nebulized bronchodilators driven by room air (rather than oxygen, to avoid delivering an uncontrolled high FiO2) significantly reduces mortality.

questions.question: In a COPD patient, inhaled corticosteroids (ICS) as monotherapy:

statements.label: A
statements.text: Leads to a slower rate of decline of lung function compared to long-acting b-agonists (LABA)

statements.label: B
statements.text: Increases the risk of osteoporosis over the next three years

statements.label: C
statements.text: Decreases the likelihood of 3-year survival compared with the use of ICS/LABA

statements.label: D
statements.text: Increases the risk of COPD exacerbation

questions.explanation: The role of ICS in COPD remains contentious despite decades of use. ICS monotherapy is more effective in asthma than in COPD, perhaps due to different pathogenesis (asthma is more eosinophil-driven, whereas COPD is more neutrophilic in origin). The large randomised TORCH study showed that the 3-year probability of death was higher in patients on ICS monotherapy compared to ICS/LABA - i.e. ICS monotherapy decreases 3-year survival relative to combination therapy. There is little evidence that ICS, or any therapy except smoking cessation, slows the rate of decline in FEV1. ICS as monotherapy does not reduce exacerbation rate more than LABA monotherapy. There is not sufficient evidence that ICS alone is independently associated with osteoporosis.

questions.question: Inhaled short-acting Beta2-sympathomimetic agents (SABA) are the mainstay therapy in acute exacerbation of asthma. Which of the following statements is/are correct?

statements.label: A
statements.text: The efficiency of the treatment depends on the route of administration - nebulizer is superior to MDI with a spacer

statements.label: B
statements.text: The efficiency of the treatment depends on the route of administration - MDI with a spacer is as effective as nebulizer

statements.label: C
statements.text: Independent of the severity of airflow obstruction, 2 doses of inhaled SABA every 6 hours are effective in the reversal of airflow obstruction

statements.label: D
statements.text: Combination inhaled therapy with SABA and anticholinergics results in reduced hospitalisation and improved lung function in patients presenting to the ED with severe asthma exacerbations

questions.explanation: Delivery of SABA via a metered-dose inhaler (MDI) with a spacer is as effective as delivery via nebulizer for reversal of airflow obstruction, and nebulizer is not superior. The required SABA dose and dosing interval depend on the severity of airflow obstruction, so a fixed low-frequency regimen independent of severity is not appropriate. Adding an inhaled anticholinergic to SABA in patients presenting to the ED with severe asthma exacerbation reduces hospitalisation rates and improves lung function compared with SABA alone.
questions.topic: SABA delivery route and combination therapy

questions.question: A 60 year-old patient with a previous history of COPD was intubated due to acute exacerbation of COPD. While he is stable, minute ventilation alarm is activated, and subsequently the patient became hypotensive and hypoxemic (SaO2 89%). He was suctioned and had minimal secretion. You look at ventilator waveforms. From up to the bottom, waveforms of Paw, Flow and volume. Waveforms in gray represent those observed just before the patient's deterioration. The most likely cause of this deterioration is:
questions.explanation: Inspection of the Paw, volume and flow waveforms reveals a loss of pressure in the system (note the decrease in Ppeak on the pressure-time waveform). While the set inspiratory volume is 500 mL, the expiratory volume is less than half that. Of the choices given, rupture of the endotracheal tube cuff is the best explanation. Other causes of loss of pressure and expired volume could be partial circuit disconnection or bronchopleural fistula. A tension pneumothorax would raise airway pressure. A pulmonary embolus has minimal effect on respiratory mechanics, though it may sometimes increase resistance, which would lead to an increase (not a decrease) in peak airway pressure. Acute mucus plugging would also raise peak airway pressure due to increased inspiratory resistance.
questions.topic: ventilator waveform interpretation - loss of circuit pressure

questions.question: Intrinsic PEEP (PEEPi) is:

statements.label: A
statements.text: Measured by subtraction of set PEEP from the plateau (Pplat) pressure

statements.label: B
statements.text: The lowest average alveolar pressure during the respiratory cycle

statements.label: C
statements.text: Measured during an end-expiratory hold manoeuvre

statements.label: D
statements.text: Normally 5-10 cmH2O

questions.explanation: Intrinsic PEEP (auto-PEEP, PEEPi) is the positive alveolar pressure that persists at end-expiration due to incomplete lung emptying, and represents the lowest average alveolar pressure reached during the respiratory cycle. It is measured with an end-expiratory hold manoeuvre (occlusion of the expiratory port just before the next inspiration), reading the plateau pressure that develops - not by subtracting set PEEP from Pplat, which reflects total respiratory system compliance instead. Unlike set (extrinsic) PEEP, PEEPi has no fixed normal range; in health it is close to zero, while in obstructive lung disease with dynamic hyperinflation it can be substantially elevated.

questions.question: Several benefits have been proven by the use of non-invasive ventilation in the treatment of severe exacerbations of COPD. The single most compelling reason for this choice is to:
options: Reduce the need for additive sedation in the patient
questions.explanation: A meta-analysis of 17 randomised controlled trials involving 1264 participants showed that, compared to standard care alone, the use of non-invasive ventilation (BiPAP modality) significantly decreases hospital mortality in patients with severe exacerbation of COPD (Cochrane Database Syst Rev. 2017 Jul 13;7:CD004104. doi: 10.1002/14651858.CD004104.pub4).
questions.topic: benefits of NIV in severe COPD exacerbation

questions.question: The end-inspiratory volume above FRC (Vei) has been shown to be predictive of the complications of hyperinflation (hypotension and barotrauma). Hyperinflation may be measured directly or by surrogate measures (indirectly) in the clinical setting by the following methods:

statements.label: A
statements.text: Total exhaled volume (over 60 secs of apnoea)

statements.label: B
statements.text: Peak inspiratory pressure

statements.label: C
statements.text: Plateau pressure

statements.label: D
statements.text: Intrinsic PEEP

questions.explanation: The end-inspiratory volume above FRC (Vei) can be measured directly as the total volume exhaled during a prolonged (about 60-second) apnoea from end-inspiration. It can also be estimated indirectly via surrogate markers of static hyperinflation such as the plateau pressure and intrinsic PEEP, both of which rise as hyperinflation worsens. Peak inspiratory pressure is influenced substantially by airway resistance and flow rate, not only by hyperinflation, so it is not a reliable surrogate for Vei.

questions.question: A 39 year-old woman with a previous history of severe asthma is on the 2nd day of mechanical ventilation on deep sedation. She was intubated due to acute respiratory failure following an acute exacerbation. Ventilator settings are as follows: Volume Control, FiO2 0.4, VT (7 mL/kg IBW), RR 27 br/min. PEEP 0 cmH2O, inspiratory:expiratory ratio 1:2, inspiratory time (pause time) 0.7 sec. With these settings, arterial blood gases (ABG) are: pH 7.46, PCO2 35 mmHg, PO2 79 mmHg. Three hours later, a new measurement of ABG reveals a significant increase in PaCO2, from 35 to 60 mmHg. At this time peak inspiratory pressure (Ppeak) and end-inspiratory pressure (Pplat) are 57 cmH2O and 41 cmH2O, respectively. Which is the most appropriate change in ventilator settings to improve PaCO2?
options: Change to pressure control with the same ventilator settings
Administer neuromuscular blockers and keep the same ventilator settings
questions.explanation: The inspiratory pause pressure gradient (Ppeak-Pplat = 16 cmH2O) is indicative of processes causing decreased inspiratory system compliance; in this patient, the decrease in respiratory system compliance is due to dynamic hyperinflation (DH). During volume-control ventilation, the development of DH gradually increases Peak and Pplat and may increase dead space, which eventually leads to a rise in PaCO2, as seen here. The main determinants of DH are high minute ventilation, a short expiratory time, and a long expiratory time constant. To decrease DH, the appropriate action is to decrease minute ventilation (by reducing respiratory rate or tidal volume) and to shorten inspiratory time (including eliminating inspiratory pause time). Administering paralytics in this patient will not help decrease DH, since she is already heavily sedated with no spontaneous breaths; furthermore, neuromuscular blockers combined with high-dose corticosteroids may lead to prolonged ventilator dependency due to progressive myopathy. Changing to pressure control with the same minute ventilation will not affect DH.

questions.question: Which of the following types of patient-ventilator asynchrony are likely to be present in a COPD mechanically ventilated patient?

statements.label: A
statements.text: Triggering delay

statements.label: B
statements.text: Ineffective efforts

statements.label: C
statements.text: Auto triggering

statements.label: D
statements.text: Delayed opening of the expiratory valve

questions.explanation: In mechanically ventilated patients with obstructive lung disease and dynamic hyperinflation, at the beginning of a breath the inspiratory muscles start contracting at volumes above passive FRC, where alveolar pressure is positive (PEEPi). To trigger the ventilator the patient must first counterbalance PEEPi to bring alveolar pressure below external PEEPe; a portion of inspiratory muscle pressure is therefore dissipated against this elastic threshold load, producing a delay between the start of inspiratory effort and triggering. In some cases the inspiratory effort cannot overcome PEEPi at all, resulting in a failure to trigger the ventilator (ineffective effort). Auto-triggering refers to the ventilator triggering in the absence of any patient effort; it may occur with any triggering mode when end-expiratory flow reaches zero for some time before the next inspiration, usually when respiratory drive and rate are low. This phenomenon rarely occurs in mechanically ventilated COPD patients, because dynamic hyperinflation means expiratory flow is rarely zero. In patients with a long expiratory time constant, such as those with COPD, delayed opening of the expiratory valve is the main type of expiratory asynchrony.

questions.question: In a patient with acute exacerbation of COPD on assisted mechanical ventilation, if you know (have measured) the PEEPi, the applied (external) PEEP (PEEPe) should be:
questions.explanation: In mechanically ventilated patients with obstructive lung disease and dynamic hyperinflation, applying external PEEP (PEEPe) substantially increases trigger sensitivity by narrowing the difference between alveolar pressure and mouth pressure at end-expiration, and it repeatedly demonstrably reduces the elastic work of breathing due to PEEPi. This benefit is most evident in patients with flow limitation during tidal expiration: in these patients expiratory flow is already maximal (wave-speed has been reached), so pressure disturbances downstream cannot propagate upstream, and applying PEEP up to a point does not affect expiratory flow or cause further hyperinflation - it merely reduces the alveolar-to-mouth pressure difference at end-expiration and raises trigger sensitivity by an amount equal to the applied PEEP. The current consensus is that PEEPe should be set at about 80% of PEEPi (i.e. 20% less than PEEPi), giving substantial relief of inspiratory workload without risking further hyperinflation.
questions.topic: setting external PEEP relative to PEEPi

questions.question: A 75-year-old man with COPD (GOLD stage 3) presented to the emergency department complaining of shortness of breath, increased sputum expectoration, and fever over the last four days, and mentions a recent hospitalisation for COPD exacerbation. On presentation: heart rate 120/min, respiratory rate 34/min, arterial pressure 150/70 mmHg, temperature 38.7°C, use of accessory respiratory muscles, and he appears slightly confused; chest auscultation reveals bilaterally diffuse wheezing rhonchi and a prolonged expiratory phase. He is intubated and mechanically ventilated in a controlled mode, heavily sedated with no spontaneous breathing effort. Regarding strategies to minimise dynamic hyperinflation (DH) in this patient during controlled mechanical ventilation, indicate whether each statement is TRUE or FALSE:

statements.label: A
statements.text: Decreasing minute ventilation (by reducing tidal volume and/or respiratory rate) reduces DH

statements.label: B
statements.text: Prolonging inspiratory time reduces DH

statements.label: C
statements.text: A tidal volume ≤6 mL/kg ideal body weight is a reasonable ventilator setting to limit DH

statements.label: D
statements.text: Administering neuromuscular blockade is an effective strategy to reduce DH in this heavily sedated, passive patient

questions.explanation: [CONSTRUCTED] Built from an ESICM course case-presentation/self-assessment slide set (interactive scenario, not a scored Final Assessment MCQ) rather than transcribed verbatim from a graded quiz item - verify against the original source before use in a graded context. Minimising dynamic hyperinflation is a key management goal in mechanically ventilated COPD patients. Three strategies reduce DH: decreasing minute ventilation, increasing expiratory time, and decreasing resistance to expiratory flow - so it is shortening, not prolonging, inspiratory time that helps. Suggested controlled-mode settings to limit DH include tidal volume ≤6 mL/kg ideal body weight, respiratory rate below 12-14/min, an inspiratory:total cycle time ratio below 0.3, and accepting permissive hypercapnia (pH >7.20-7.25) where not contraindicated. In a heavily sedated, passive patient with no spontaneous respiratory effort, DH results entirely from the ventilator settings rather than from patient effort, so neuromuscular blockade does not reduce DH - and combining paralytics with high-dose corticosteroids risks precipitating critical illness myopathy and prolonging ventilator dependency.

questions.question: The Heliox is used as a treatment in severe asthma exacerbation. Which of the following statements are correct?

statements.label: A
statements.text: The Heliox decreases airway flow resistance by relaxing the airway smooth muscle

statements.label: B
statements.text: The Heliox reduces airflow resistance by facilitating the transmission of laminar to turbulence flow in distal airways

statements.label: C
statements.text: Heliox therapy should be considered in severe hypoxaemic patients (requiring supplemental O2, with FiO2 > 50%) that are unresponsive to standard therapy.

statements.label: D
statements.text: Heliox therapy is not suitable in severe hypoxaemic patients, requiring supplemental O2, with FiO2 > 50%

questions.explanation: Heliox has no direct bronchodilator/smooth-muscle-relaxing effect; its benefit is purely physical. Because helium is far less dense than nitrogen, replacing nitrogen with helium promotes a shift from turbulent to laminar flow in narrowed distal airways (not the reverse), which reduces the pressure needed to generate a given flow and so reduces the work of breathing. This density-dependent benefit requires a high fraction of helium in the gas mixture; once FiO2 needs to exceed about 40-50% the proportion of helium is too low for the effect to persist, so Heliox is not a suitable therapy for severely hypoxaemic patients who need a high FiO2.

questions.question: In patients with acute exacerbation of COPD requiring mechanical ventilation, the following factors are associated with poor long-term outcome

statements.label: A
statements.text: Dyspnoea at rest with hypoxaemia and hypercapnia

statements.label: B
statements.text: Reversible airway obstruction after treatment with inhaled β-adrenergic agonists

statements.label: C
statements.text: Hyperalbuminemia

statements.label: D
statements.text: Previous history of several acute exacerbations in the history

questions.explanation: Persistent dyspnoea at rest with hypoxaemia and hypercapnia, and a history of multiple previous acute exacerbations, both identify a more severe COPD phenotype and are associated with a poorer long-term prognosis after an episode requiring mechanical ventilation. Airway obstruction that is reversible with inhaled beta-agonists is a favourable feature (more asthma-like physiology) rather than a marker of poor outcome. Hyperalbuminemia is not a recognised prognostic factor - if anything, hypoalbuminaemia, reflecting malnutrition and chronic illness burden, is associated with worse outcomes.
questions.topic: prognostic factors after mechanically ventilated AECOPD

questions.question: Which of the following are true pertaining to the pathophysiologic factors that are associated with atelectasis formation in mechanically ventilated COPD patients?

statements.label: A
statements.text: Administration of High O2 concentration

statements.label: B
statements.text: Increased diaphragmatic contractility due to diaphragm flattening

statements.label: C
statements.text: Administration of Low O2 concentration leads to high differences in the partial gas pressures between alveoli and venous (pulmonary arterial) blood, which in turn promotes the development of adsorption atelectasis

statements.label: D
statements.text: Accumulation of bronchial secretions may lead to airway obstruction

questions.explanation: Administration of a high (not low) inspired oxygen concentration washes out alveolar nitrogen; when a distal airway becomes obstructed, the remaining oxygen is rapidly absorbed into the blood, causing the alveolus to collapse - this is absorption atelectasis, and it is high, not low, FiO2 that promotes it. Diaphragm flattening, as occurs with hyperinflation in COPD, places the diaphragm at a mechanical disadvantage and reduces rather than increases its contractile efficiency. Accumulation of bronchial secretions can obstruct airways and lead to distal atelectasis through gas resorption behind the obstruction.
questions.topic: atelectasis mechanisms in ventilated COPD patients

questions.question: Inhaled short-acting b-adrenergic agonists (SABA) are considered the cornerstone in the treatment of mechanically ventilated COPD and asthma patients. Which of the following statements is correct?
options: The combination of inhaled SABA and inhaled fluticasone is more effective in the reversal of airway obstruction than inhaled SABA as monotherapy
Inhaled SABA as monotherapy is as effective as inhaled corticosteroids as monotherapy in the reversal of airway obstruction
The duration of action of inhaled bronchodilators during mechanical ventilation is equal to that in ambulatory patients
The efficiency of drug delivery for inhaled bronchodilators is independent of the severity of airway obstruction
The doses of inhaled bronchodilators during mechanical ventilation should be higher than that suggested for ambulatory patients
questions.explanation: During mechanical ventilation, drug delivery efficiency from inhaled devices is markedly reduced by factors such as the endotracheal tube, ventilator circuit, humidification, and altered breath characteristics, so a much smaller fraction of the nominal dose reaches the lower airways than in an ambulatory patient using the same device. As a result, higher and/or more frequent doses of inhaled bronchodilators are needed during mechanical ventilation to achieve an equivalent clinical effect, and the duration of bronchodilator action is correspondingly shorter than in ambulatory patients.
questions.topic: inhaled bronchodilator delivery during mechanical ventilation

questions.question: Which of the following is a recommended intervention to reduce the risk of VAP?

statements.label: A
statements.text: Nursing in the semirecumbent position

statements.label: B
statements.text: Selective digestive decontamination

statements.label: C
statements.text: Selective oropharynx and digestive decontamination

statements.label: D
statements.text: Use of subglottic secretions drainage-endotracheal tubes

questions.explanation: Nursing mechanically ventilated patients in the semirecumbent (30-45°) position and using endotracheal tubes with subglottic secretion drainage are both established measures within standard VAP-prevention bundles. Selective digestive decontamination and selective oropharyngeal/digestive decontamination are not part of the standard, widely recommended VAP-prevention bundle in this context.

questions.question: Which of the following statements are correct for the use of inhaled corticosteroids in mechanically ventilated patients with COPD and asthma?

statements.label: A
statements.text: The combination of inhaled corticosteroids and inhaled b-adrenergic agonists is more effective in the reversal of airway obstruction than inhaled b-adrenergic agonists as monotherapy

statements.label: B
statements.text: Inhaled corticosteroids four times a day is as effective as systematic corticosteroids

statements.label: C
statements.text: The combination of inhaled corticosteroids and inhaled b-adrenergic agonists are considered as the standard therapy

statements.label: D
statements.text: Current evidence does not support the use of inhaled corticosteroids as standard therapy in mechanically ventilated patients with COPD and asthma

questions.explanation: In mechanically ventilated patients with COPD and asthma, current evidence does not support inhaled corticosteroids - alone or combined with an inhaled beta-agonist - as standard therapy: they are not shown to add meaningfully to bronchodilator-driven reversal of airway obstruction in this setting, are not equivalent to systemic corticosteroids however frequently dosed, and are not part of the established standard-of-care regimen, which instead relies on systemic corticosteroids alongside bronchodilators.

questions.question: The mortality rate of COPD patients requiring mechanical ventilation for an acute exacerbation is:
questions.explanation: [UNCONFIRMED] The source screenshot only shows the selected answer, '35-50% in three years', marked incorrect; no correct option was visibly highlighted and no feedback text was captured for this item. Best available estimate: COPD patients requiring mechanical ventilation for an acute exacerbation have a reported six-month mortality in the range of roughly 40-70%, consistent with other ESICM course material in this bank on the same topic. Verify against the original ESICM material if possible.
